name: scic_sds_abort_reqests
prose: Precondition: controller is non-NULL; remote_device and port may each be NULL. request_count starts as remote_device->started_request_count when remote_device is non-NULL, else port->started_request_count when port is non-NULL, else SCI_MAX_IO_REQUESTS. It scans controller->io_request_table from index 0 while index < SCI_MAX_IO_REQUESTS and request_count > 0. For each non-NULL entry it tests whether the request's target_device equals remote_device, or the target_device's owning_port equals port (this dereferences target_device whenever the first test is false, so target_device must be non-NULL in that case), or both remote_device and port are NULL; for each match it calls scic_controller_terminate_request(controller, target_device, request), remembers the last non-SCI_SUCCESS status it returned, and decrements request_count. Matching entries are terminated whether or not they were started, and matching entries beyond the first request_count matches are not visited once request_count reaches 0. It returns SCI_SUCCESS if no terminate call failed (including when none was made), otherwise the last failing status. It takes no locks.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the second clause at scic_sds_controller.c:6902 dereferences target_device->owning_port even when only port is non-NULL and remote_device is NULL (or whenever target_device != remote_device). Round 2 reviewer right that the port count is used only when remote_device is NULL (6885-6890); round 1 right that non-started matches may be terminated and the scan stops at request_count. Real function at 6873-6920 (slice 6720-6972). Read in full; scic_controller_terminate_request not read.

name: scic_sds_io_sequence_increment
note: Function-like macro at scic_sds_controller.h:572-573, ((value) = (((value) + 1) & 0x000F)); it only computes and assigns an expression and defines no function.

name: scic_sds_phy_starting_substate_await_iaf_uf_frame_handler
prose: Precondition: this_phy is a valid phy in the AWAIT_IAF_UF starting substate and frame_index names an unsolicited frame of the controller. It obtains the frame header with scic_sds_unsolicited_frame_control_get_header; if that returns an error it returns that error at once and does not release the frame. Otherwise it byte-swaps header word 0 (this happens before the frame-type test). If the address frame type is 0 (identify frame) it also byte-swaps words 1 to 5, copies the frame into this_phy's identify_address_frame_buffer, and changes the starting substate to FINAL if the frame's protocols have the SMP target bit set, or to AWAIT_SAS_POWER otherwise. If the type is non-zero it only logs a warning and copies nothing and does not change the substate. In both of those cases it releases the frame with scic_sds_controller_release_frame and returns SCI_SUCCESS (the value from get_header).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: word 0 is swapped unconditionally (scic_sds_phy.c:3205), words 1-5 only for type 0 (3212-3216). Original reviewer right on the get_header failure not releasing the frame (3200-3203); an unexpected frame type returns SCI_SUCCESS without copying or advancing (3244-3259). Real function at 3186-3260 (slice 3195-3495). Read in full.

name: scic_sds_port_decrement_request_count
note: In this header it is declared as a function only under SCIC_DEBUG_ENABLED (scic_sds_port.h:308-310, defined elsewhere); otherwise it is the function-like macro at 316-323 that only computes and assigns the new count (decrement unless 0). The item shown is a macro or a declaration, not a function defined in this file.

name: scic_remote_device_da_construct
prose: Precondition: remote_device was set up with scic_remote_device_construct and has a valid owning port. It records the port's attached protocols in target_protocols, sets is_direct_attached to TRUE, sets is_atapi (unless DISABLE_ATAPI is defined), and sets device_port_width to the number of bits set in the port's phy_mask; these happen before the allocation. It then calls scic_sds_controller_allocate_remote_node_context; if that returns a status other than SCI_SUCCESS it returns that status, and the remote node index, device address, ready substate machine, connection rate and the final port width of 1 are not set (but the protocols, direct-attached flag, atapi flag and phy-mask port width were already changed). On SCI_SUCCESS it stores the allocated index in the RNC, copies the port's attached SAS address into device_address, then sets has_ready_substate_machine to FALSE for an SSP target, or to TRUE and constructs the STP ready substate machine for an STP target, or the SMP one for an SMP target (checked in that order; if none of the three target bits is set the flag is not changed), sets connection_rate to the port's maximum allowed speed, sets device_port_width to 1 and returns SCI_SUCCESS.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: device_port_width is already set from the phy mask at scic_sds_remote_device.c:169-171 before the allocation, so it is not unchanged on failure. Original reviewer right that SSP builds no ready substate machine (189-192). Read in full at 140-226.

name: scic_remote_device_ea_construct
prose: Precondition: remote_device is a constructed device with a valid owning port and discover_response points to an SMP DISCOVER response for the attached target. It fills the device's target information from the response with scic_sds_remote_device_get_info_from_smp_discover_response, then calls scic_sds_controller_allocate_remote_node_context passing the address of this_device->rnc->remote_node_index; if that returns a status other than SCI_SUCCESS it returns that status and does nothing more (the discover-response information has already been recorded). On SCI_SUCCESS it sets has_ready_substate_machine to FALSE for an SSP target, or to TRUE and constructs the SMP ready substate machine for an SMP target, or the STP one for an STP target (checked in that order; if no bit is set the flag is unchanged), sets connection_rate to the minimum of the port's maximum allowed speed and the response's negotiated physical link rate, sets device_port_width to 1 and returns SCI_SUCCESS.
note: Packet name scic_remote_device_ea_sas_construct does not exist in the source; the real function is scic_remote_device_ea_construct at scic_sds_remote_device.c:249-327 (the name ea_sas_construct appears only in a log string at 265). Read in full. Whether the allocation routine writes the index through the pointer even on failure was not read.

name: scic_sds_remote_node_context_get_remote_node_index
note: Function-like macro at scic_sds_remote_node_context.h:341-342; it only forwards to ((rnc)->remote_node_index) (its parameter is named rcn, so the body uses a free rnc), no function is defined.

name: scic_sds_stp_remote_device_ready_substate_start_request_handler
prose: Precondition: device is a valid STP remote device in a READY substate and request is a valid request. It calls the owning port's start_io_handler; if that returns a status other than SCI_SUCCESS it returns that status and does nothing else. If it succeeds it calls scic_sds_remote_node_context_start_task on the RNC, and, only if that succeeds, the request's parent start_handler. Only when both succeed (status is SCI_SUCCESS) does it set working_request to the request, change the ready substate to CMD, and suspend the RNC (SCI_SOFTWARE_SUSPENSION) and resume it with scic_sds_remote_device_continue_request as the callback. In every case where the port's start_io succeeded (including when the RNC start or the parent start failed) it then calls scic_sds_remote_device_start_request(this_device, this_request, status) with the current status, and returns SCI_FAILURE_RESET_DEVICE_PARTIAL_SUCCESS.
note: Both reviewers right: scic_sds_remote_device_start_request and the PARTIAL_SUCCESS return are outside the inner 'status == SCI_SUCCESS' block, inside the port start_io success block (scic_sds_stp_remote_device.c:176-218), so they run even if the RNC or parent start failed. Function at 160-222. Read in full.

name: scic_cb_io_request_complete
prose: Precondition: controller, remote_device and io_request each have an associated framework object (sci_object_get_association). It calls the request's state_handlers->complete_handler. If that returns anything other than SCI_SUCCESS nothing further happens. If it returns SCI_SUCCESS: when the request's protocol_complete_handler is non-NULL it is called with the controller, device, request and a pointer to completion_status (the handler may change completion_status), and its result becomes status; when the handler is NULL, status stays SCI_SUCCESS. If status is SCI_SUCCESS, a request that is not high priority and not waiting for the abort task set is completed to the user with scif_cb_io_request_complete using completion_status; a request that is not high priority but is waiting for the abort task set is left untouched; a high-priority request is passed to scif_sas_controller_complete_high_priority_io (regardless of the abort-task-set flag). If status is SCI_WARNING_SEQUENCE_INCOMPLETE the IO is continued with scif_sas_io_request_continue. For any other status nothing more is done. The function returns nothing.
note: Both reviewers right: with is_waiting_for_abort_task_set set and not high priority neither completion is called (scif_sas_io_request.c:444-456), and the NULL protocol_complete_handler case keeps status SCI_SUCCESS (433-442). Function at 402-466 (slice 255-506). Read in full.

name: isp_fclink_test
prose: Precondition: chan is a valid channel and usdelay is the firmware-ready wait in microseconds. It returns -1 if the channel's loop state is below LOOP_HAVE_LINK, and 0 at once (doing nothing) if it is already at or beyond LOOP_LTEST_DONE. Otherwise it repeatedly reads the firmware state (sleeping 1 ms between tries) until it is FW_READY or about usdelay microseconds have passed; if the loop state drops below LOOP_HAVE_LINK during this wait it logs and returns 1; if the firmware state is not FW_READY afterwards it returns -1. It then issues MBOX_GET_LOOP_ID, returning -1 if the command does not complete. It records the topology (set to TOPO_PTP_STUB if the reported value is outside the range TOPO_NL_PORT..TOPO_PTP_STUB), the port ID, and, for a non-fabric topology the loop ID, or for a fabric topology other than F port the loop ID found by looking up the ALPA in alpa_map if found. It sets the loop state to LOOP_TESTING_LINK. For TOPO_F_PORT or TOPO_FL_PORT it queries the fabric controller port database; if that query fails or gives port ID 0 it forces topology to TOPO_PTP_STUB and skips the fabric steps; otherwise it stores the fabric params and SNS handle and tries the FC4 type, FC4 feature, port name and node name registrations in turn: if the loop state falls below LOOP_TESTING_LINK after any of them it logs and returns 1, and if one of the first three returns nonzero it skips the remaining registrations (the registration failure does not change the topology and the function can still return 0). It then sets isp_gbspeed to 1 and updates it from the MBOX_GET_SET_DATA_RATE reply when that command completes. If the loop state is below LOOP_TESTING_LINK at that point it logs and returns 1; otherwise it sets the loop state to LOOP_LTEST_DONE, logs the link information and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: out-of-range mailbox topology is clamped to TOPO_PTP_STUB (isp.c:1701-1703), and fabric params and SNS handle are set only on the F/FL port path after a good PDB query (1734-1735). Round 2 right: forcing TOPO_PTP_STUB happens only when the PDB query fails (1727-1731); round 1 right about the abort return 1 during the firmware wait (1677-1678). Function at 1650-1798 (slice 1600-1873). Read in full.

name: isp_gdt
prose: Precondition: arg is a pointer to a valid struct isp_fc whose gtask task has been initialised (TASK_INIT with isp_gdt_task), and the structure stays valid until the task runs. This is the callout function: it only calls taskqueue_enqueue(taskqueue_thread, &fc->gtask) and returns nothing. It does not take the ISP lock, scan the port database or re-arm the callout itself; those actions are done later by the separate task function isp_gdt_task.
note: Both reviewers (original and round 15) described isp_gdt_task (isp_freebsd.c:2044-2093, which takes ISP_LOCK, scans portdb and re-arms or deactivates the callout when fc->ready), because the slice 2054-2304 started inside that function; isp_gdt itself is the three-line function at 2036-2041 and the old prose for it is correct. Both reviewer claims are about a different function, so they do not apply to isp_gdt. Read both functions in full.

name: isp_reset
prose: Precondition: isp is a valid softc for a 24xx-or-later FC adapter with register access; do_load_defaults selects whether defaults are loaded at the end. The function returns nothing; it returns early at many points after logging (or silently), leaving the adapter in whatever state it reached, with isp_state left at ISP_NILSTATE (it is set to ISP_RESETSTATE only at the end). It sets isp_state to ISP_NILSTATE, disables interrupts and pauses the RISC, stops DMA (polling up to 100000 x 10 us and only logging if it does not stop), soft-resets the chip and polls OUTMAILBOX0 up to 10000 times for it to leave 0x4: returns after logging if the value is 0x4 (ROM busy), 0xf (board configuration error) or an unknown value. It then resets and releases the RISC and repeats that OUTMAILBOX0 check with the same three early returns. It zeroes the request, response and ATIO indices and the queue pointer registers (the priority request pointers only when not a 26xx). It runs MBOX_NO_OP (return if it does not complete) and the mailbox register test (return if the command fails or, after logging, if any register value mismatches), then ISP_MBOXDMASETUP (return after logging on failure). Next it sets up the flash addresses, firmware version strings and, unless ISP_CFG_NORELOAD is set, tries firmware_get for the ispfw module. It decides whether to download: on 27xx via isp_load_risc (success means firmware already loaded; abort or, with ispfw present, other failures mean download), on others only if ispfw was obtained. If downloading, it loads each firmware fragment into RAM (return after logging on a load failure; the firmware reference is not released on that path) and, after all succeed, calls firmware_put with FIRMWARE_UNLOAD on the ispfw reference. If firmware was loaded it verifies the checksum (return on failure), else on 26xx asks the RISC to load from flash (return on failure). It then issues MBOX_EXEC_FIRMWARE (return if not complete), records the ability mask, issues MBOX_ABOUT_FIRMWARE (return if not complete), stores firmware revision and attributes, logs them, issues MBOX_GET_RESOURCE_COUNT (return if not complete; sets isp_maxcmds), limits isp_nchan to 1 for firmware without multi-ID or VP0 decoupling support, calls ISP_MBOXDMASETUP again and ISP_IRQSETUP (return after logging on failure), enables interrupts, sets each channel's firmware state to FW_CONFIG_WAIT, sets isp_state to ISP_RESETSTATE and, if do_load_defaults, calls isp_setdfltfcparm for each channel.
note: Packet name isp_firmware_reset_2400 does not exist; the slice 262-517 lies inside isp_reset at isp.c:206-818 (read in full; the firmware-attribute logging blocks at 617-756 were skimmed, not checked line by line). Old prose said the firmware reference remains owned by the softc on every path; in the code firmware_put is called after a successful download (525-526) and the reference stays in isp_osinfo.ispfw otherwise, so the statement was not correct for all paths. The 'DMA setup' failure path appears twice (385-388, 790-793).

name: iwi_notification_intr
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid iwi softc whose ic has at least one vap (the first vap is dereferenced in several branches) and notif points to a firmware notification whose payload is at least as long as the structure implied by notif->type. The function returns nothing and dispatches on notif->type. SCAN_CHANNEL only sets sc->sc_state_timer to 3. SCAN_COMPLETE ends the IWI_FW_SCANNING state; in monitor mode it queues sc->sc_monitortask, otherwise if scan->status is IWI_SCAN_COMPLETED it calls ieee80211_scan_next(vap). AUTHENTICATION: IWI_AUTH_SUCCESS calls ieee80211_new_state(vap, IEEE80211_S_ASSOC); IWI_AUTH_FAIL clears IWI_FLAG_ASSOCIATED and, if the vap is not in RUN state, counts is_rx_auth_fail and ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING, else counts is_rx_deauth, then calls ieee80211_new_state to SCAN; IWI_AUTH_SENT_1, IWI_AUTH_RECV_2 and IWI_AUTH_SEQ1_PASS do nothing; IWI_AUTH_SEQ1_FAIL counts is_rx_auth_fail and ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING; other states print an unknown-state message. ASSOCIATION: IWI_AUTH_SUCCESS does nothing; IWI_ASSOC_SUCCESS sets IWI_FLAG_ASSOCIATED, ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING, calls iwi_checkforqos with the association frame and calls ieee80211_new_state to RUN; IWI_ASSOC_INIT clears IWI_FLAG_ASSOCIATED and, depending on sc->fw_state, ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING and moves to SCAN (association failed), or ends IWI_FW_DISASSOCIATING, counts is_rx_disassoc and moves to SCAN, and does nothing else for other firmware states; other states print an unknown-state message. BEACON: for a beacon-miss state whose count is at least vap->iv_bmissthreshold it counts is_beacon_miss and queues sc->sc_disassoctask. CALIBRATION and NOISE only produce a debug print. LINK_QUALITY calls iwi_notif_link_quality. An unknown type only produces a debug print.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the auth sub-states IWI_AUTH_SENT_1/RECV_2/SEQ1_PASS and the association IWI_AUTH_SUCCESS case just break with no log (if_iwi.c:1457-1460, 1478-1480). Original reviewer right that SCAN_CHANNEL only resets the timer (1404). Function at 1385-1561 (slice 1268-1520). Read in full; comment-only lines and debug prints skipped, iwi_notif_link_quality not read.

name: iwn_attach
prose: Precondition: dev is a probed iwn PCI device with its softc zeroed by the bus, called once from attach. It reads the debug resource value, then calls pci_find_cap for PCI Express and returns its error directly (without iwn_detach) if nonzero; it enables bus mastering and allocates the memory BAR, returning ENOMEM directly (without iwn_detach) if that fails. It then tries to allocate one MSI vector and allocates the IRQ resource (shared when MSI was not obtained); from that point every failure jumps to the fail label, which calls iwn_detach(dev) and returns the saved error: IRQ allocation failure (ENOMEM), then after the lock init and hardware-specific attach, errors from iwn_config_specific, iwn_hw_prepare, iwn_alloc_fwmem, iwn_alloc_kw, iwn_alloc_ict (not done for the 4965), iwn_alloc_sched, any iwn_alloc_tx_ring, iwn_alloc_rx_ring, iwn_read_eeprom, taskqueue_start_threads and bus_setup_intr. On the success path it also clears pending interrupts, fills in the ieee80211com capabilities (HT capabilities only when IWN_FLAG_HAS_11N is set), calls ieee80211_ifattach and saves/overrides the ampdu, addba, wme and other net80211 callbacks, attaches radiotap, initialises the three callouts and the rftoggle, panic and xmit tasks and the transmit mbuf queue, creates and starts the taskqueue, attaches sysctls, installs the interrupt handler, optionally announces the device, creates the debug character device (if make_dev returns NULL only a message is printed; otherwise si_drv1 is set to the softc) and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: iwn_read_eeprom failure also goes to fail and calls iwn_detach (if_iwn.c:588-591), and the old prose omitted it and the IRQ-allocation failure (476-479). Real function at 422-733 (slice 553-853 cut the head). Read in full except debug prints and the large capability/callback assignments, which were skimmed; iwn_detach not read, so what it releases is not described.

name: iwn_scan
prose: Precondition: sc, vap (with valid iv_bss and iv_ifp) and ss are non-NULL: ss is tested against NULL once when copying the SSID, but it is dereferenced unconditionally later (ss->ss_nssid when setting the channel flags and when computing the dwell time), so a NULL ss would fault. The argument c is ignored: it is replaced by ic->ic_curchan. If sc->sc_is_scanning is already set it prints a message and returns EAGAIN with no other effect. Otherwise it sets sc->rxon to &sc->rx_on[IWN_RXON_BSS_CTX], then allocates the scan buffer (M_NOWAIT); on failure it returns ENOMEM (sc->rxon has already been assigned). It builds the scan header, a TX template with a broadcast probe request (SSID, rates and, if HT, HT capabilities) and one channel entry for the current channel with active or passive flags and dwell times, sets sc->sc_is_scanning to 1, sends the command with iwn_cmd(sc, IWN_CMD_SCAN, buf, buflen, 1), frees the buffer, arms sc->scan_timeout for 5 seconds only if iwn_cmd returned 0, and returns iwn_cmd's result. In this function sc_is_scanning is not reset if iwn_cmd fails, so it stays 1 after any path that got past the buffer allocation. No lock is taken or released here.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: nothing in iwn_scan resets sc_is_scanning to 0 after an iwn_cmd failure (if_iwn.c:7372-7383); whether iwn_cmd or its caller does so was not read. Round 2 reviewer right that sc->rxon is assigned before malloc (7157-7164). Original reviewer's EAGAIN point is right (7148-7152). Real function at 7122-7384 (slice 7082-7334). Read in full.

name: iwx_run_init_mvm_ucode
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the softc mutex (sc_mtx is used with msleep) and readnvm says whether the NVM should be read. If IWX_FLAG_RFKILL is set and readnvm is 0 it prints a message and returns EPERM. Otherwise it clears sc_init_complete, calls iwx_load_ucode_wait_alive and returns its error if nonzero. It then sends the init-extended-config command and the NVM-access-complete command with iwx_send_cmd_pdu, returning the error of the first one that fails (before any wait for the init-complete flag). Only then does it wait: while IWX_INIT_COMPLETE is not set in sc_init_complete it calls msleep on sc_init_complete (with sc_mtx, 2 second timeout) and returns the msleep error (for example a timeout) if nonzero. If readnvm is nonzero it then calls iwx_nvm_get (returning its error after printing a message) and copies the NVM hardware address into ic_macaddr. It returns 0 otherwise. The mutex is dropped during msleep and held again on every return.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: both commands are sent before waiting for IWX_INIT_COMPLETE (if_iwx.c:4068-4092). Original reviewer's point (waits for IWX_INIT_COMPLETE, not IWX_COMPLETE) matches wait_flags at 4039. Function at 4036-4107 (slice 3889-4141). Read in full; callees not read.

name: IWX_RX_QUEUE_CB_SIZE
note: Function-like macro at if_iwxreg.h:492, ((sizeof(x) <= 4) ? (fls(x) - 1) : (flsl(x) - 1)); it only computes an expression, no function is defined.

name: ixgbe_bp_set_state
prose: Precondition: arg1 is the ixgbe_softc and req is a valid sysctl request. It reads control page 0 with hw->mac.ops.bypass_rw while holding the bypass mutex (released right after) and returns that error if nonzero; it stores the status bits ((value >> BYPASS_STATUS_OFF_SHIFT) & 0x3) in a function-static variable and passes it to sysctl_handle_int; it returns that call's error, or 0 when the request carries no new value. A new value other than BYPASS_NORM, BYPASS_BYPASS or BYPASS_ISOLATE returns EINVAL. Otherwise, holding the bypass mutex, it calls bypass_set(hw, BYPASS_PAGE_CTL0, BYPASS_MODE_OFF_M, state): because of operator precedence in the assignment, a nonzero result of that call makes error equal 1 (not the driver's error code) and it skips the second call; if it succeeds it calls bypass_set again with BYPASS_AUTO and returns that call's error code. The mutex is released at the out label on both of these paths, followed by a 6 ms delay, and the function returns error.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: 'if ((error = bypass_set(...) != 0))' at if_bypass.c:184-186 assigns the comparison result 1 to error. Original reviewer right that the sysctl_handle_int error is returned (170-172) and that the EINVAL check exists. Real function at 154-194 (slice 1-254). Read in full.

name: ixgbe_setup_mac_link_smartspeed
prose: Precondition: hw is a valid ixgbe_hw. It reads AUTOC once at entry, sets hw->phy.autoneg_advertised from the 10G, 1G and 100M full-duplex bits of speed, and sets smart_speed_active to false. Then for up to IXGBE_SMARTSPEED_MAX_RETRIES rounds it calls ixgbe_setup_mac_link_82599 and polls ixgbe_check_link 5 times at 100 ms intervals; an error from either call, or link up, ends the function immediately and returns that status (IXGBE_SUCCESS when link came up) with smart_speed_active false. If no link came up in those rounds and the AUTOC value read at entry lacks KR support or lacks KX4/KX support, it returns the last status (IXGBE_SUCCESS) without any further attempt (no link may exist). Otherwise it sets smart_speed_active to true, calls ixgbe_setup_mac_link_82599 again (an error is returned with smart_speed_active still true) and polls ixgbe_check_link 6 times at 100 ms: an error or link up returns that status with smart_speed_active still true. If still no link it sets smart_speed_active back to false, calls ixgbe_setup_mac_link_82599 once more and returns its status. A message is logged if the link is up at 1 Gb/s.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: smart_speed_active stays true on the error returns after it is set (ixgbe_82599.c:868-872, 884-886), not only on a successful KR-disabled retry. Original reviewer right that IXGBE_SUCCESS is returned without a link in the no-KR/KX case (863-865). Function at 800-902 (slice 763-1013). Read in full.

name: ixgbe_identify_sfp_module_generic
prose: Precondition: hw is a valid ixgbe_hw with mac and phy ops set. It remembers the current sfp_type. If the media type is not fiber it sets phy.sfp_type to not_present and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_PRESENT (phy.id and phy.type are not changed on this path). Otherwise it calls set_lan_id and reads the identifier byte over I2C; if any of the checked I2C reads (identifier, 1G and 10G compliance codes, cable technology, and the three vendor OUI bytes when phy.type is not ixgbe_phy_nl) returns nonzero it goes to a common error exit that sets sfp_type to not_present, zeroes phy.id and sets phy.type to ixgbe_phy_unknown unless phy.type is ixgbe_phy_nl, and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_PRESENT (not the read's own error code). If the identifier is not IXGBE_SFF_IDENTIFIER_SFP it sets phy.type to ixgbe_phy_sfp_unsupported and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_SUPPORTED. Otherwise it sets phy.sfp_type from the cable type and compliance codes (on 82598 only DA passive, SR, LR or unknown; on others core 0 or core 1 variants depending on lan_id; the cable-spec read for active DA cables is not checked), sets sfp_setup_needed if sfp_type changed, sets multispeed_fiber, and unless phy.type is ixgbe_phy_nl records the identifier as phy.id and sets phy.type from the vendor OUI. Then: a DA passive or active cable returns IXGBE_SUCCESS; a module with 10G compliance 0 whose sfp_type is not one of the 1G types sets phy.type to ixgbe_phy_sfp_unsupported and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_SUPPORTED; an 82598 returns IXGBE_SUCCESS; otherwise it reads the device caps and, unless IXGBE_DEVICE_CAPS_ALLOW_ANY_SFP is set or the type is a 1G type, accepts only Intel modules (IXGBE_SUCCESS) or, when hw->allow_unsupported_sfp is true, accepts with a one-time warning; else sets phy.type unsupported and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_SUPPORTED. All remaining cases return IXGBE_SUCCESS.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: the err_read_i2c_eeprom exit returns the fixed IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_PRESENT (ixgbe_phy.c:1575-1581), not the read error. Original reviewer right that the unchecked cable-spec read (1381-1383) can fail while the function still succeeds. The non-fiber path leaves phy.type and phy.id untouched. Real function at 1291-1582 (slice 1265-1515 cut the head). Read in full (debug macros skipped); ixgbe_get_device_caps not read.

name: ixgbe_check_mac_link_vf
prose: Precondition: hw, speed and link_up are valid pointers (autoneg_wait_to_complete is unused). It sets mac->get_link_status to true if check_for_rst (mailbox ops[0]) returns 0 or mbx->timeout is 0. If get_link_status is false it skips to the exit. Otherwise it reads VFLINKS and exits if the link-up bit is clear; for the 82599 VF it re-reads VFLINKS five times at 100 us and exits if the link-up bit clears at any point. Past those checks it sets *speed from the speed bits of the last VFLINKS value (10G, or 2.5G on X550 or later with the non-standard bit; 1G; 100M, or 5G on X550/E610 VF with the non-standard bit; 10M on X550 or later for the X550EM_A 10M code; otherwise IXGBE_LINK_SPEED_UNKNOWN). It then reads one mailbox word with ixgbe_read_mbx: if that fails, get_link_status is cleared only when hw->api_version >= ixgbe_mbox_api_15, and the function exits with ret_val unchanged (IXGBE_SUCCESS); if the reply lacks IXGBE_VT_MSGTYPE_CTS it sets ret_val to IXGBE_ERR_MBX only when the FAILURE bit is also set, else leaves IXGBE_SUCCESS, and exits; if CTS is present and mbx->timeout is 0 it sets ret_val to IXGBE_ERR_TIMEOUT and exits; otherwise it clears get_link_status. At the exit it sets *link_up to !mac->get_link_status and returns ret_val. *speed is written only on the path that reached the speed decode; on other paths it is left unchanged.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: IXGBE_ERR_TIMEOUT is returned when CTS is present and mbx->timeout is 0 (ixgbe_vf.c:692-695), not when CTS is missing. Original reviewer right that *speed is not set when get_link_status is already false (623-624). Function at 608-705 (slice 508-760). Read in full.

name: i40e_aq_debug_dump
prose: Precondition: hw is a valid hardware structure; ret_buff_size, ret_next_table and ret_next_index may each be NULL. It returns I40E_ERR_PARAM, without sending anything, if buff_size is 0 or buff is NULL. Otherwise it fills a default descriptor for the i40e_aqc_opc_debug_dump_internals opcode, sets the buffer flag (and the large-buffer flag when buff_size > I40E_AQ_LARGE_BUF), writes cluster_id, table_id and the little-endian start_index into the command, sets datalen to buff_size, and sends it with i40e_asq_send_command using buff as the data buffer. It returns that call's status. Only when the status is zero (I40E_SUCCESS) does it write each non-NULL output: *ret_buff_size from the descriptor's returned datalen, *ret_next_table from the response table_id and *ret_next_index from the response idx; on any error status none of them is written.
note: Packet name i40e_aq_debug_dump_internals does not exist; the real function is i40e_aq_debug_dump at i40e_common.c:6244-6284 (read in full; the name i40e_aqc_debug_dump_internals is a command structure). Old prose called it an indirect command; the code sets the buffer flag I40E_AQ_FLAG_BUF (6263). i40e_asq_send_command not read.

name: i40e_remove_pd_page
prose: Precondition: hw and hmc_info are valid pointers and idx is a valid index into hmc_info->sd_table.sd_entry; hmc_info is dereferenced by the callee, so it must not be NULL. It calls i40e_prep_remove_pd_page(hmc_info, idx). If that does not return I40E_SUCCESS it returns I40E_SUCCESS (the initial value) without calling the second step; the prep call itself returns I40E_ERR_NOT_READY without changing anything when the pd table's ref_cnt is nonzero, and on success marks the sd entry invalid and decrements the sd table reference count. If the prep succeeded it returns the status of i40e_remove_pd_page_new(hw, hmc_info, idx, TRUE), whose effects on registers and entries were not read.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: hmc_info is used unchecked by the prep function (i40e_hmc.c:334), so it may not be NULL; the old 'may be NULL' precondition and the claim that tables are unchanged on prep failure are replaced (a successful prep already changes sd_entry->valid and the sd refcount before the second call). Round 2 right that a failing prep still gives I40E_SUCCESS (i40e_lan_hmc.c:270-275). Function at 266-276 (slice 252-516). Read in full with i40e_prep_remove_pd_page; i40e_remove_pd_page_new not read.

name: i40e_remove_sd_bp
prose: Precondition: hw and hmc_info are valid pointers and idx is a valid index into hmc_info->sd_table.sd_entry; hmc_info is dereferenced by the callee, so it must not be NULL. It calls i40e_prep_remove_sd_bp(hmc_info, idx). That call decrements the sd entry's backing-page reference count first and, if the count is still nonzero, returns I40E_ERR_NOT_READY (the decrement stays applied); otherwise it decrements the sd table reference count, marks the entry invalid and returns I40E_SUCCESS. If prep does not return I40E_SUCCESS, i40e_remove_sd_bp returns I40E_SUCCESS (its initial value) without calling the second step; if prep succeeds it returns the status of i40e_remove_sd_bp_new(hw, hmc_info, idx, TRUE), whose effects were not read.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right on the NULL hmc_info; round 2 right that a failing prep still returns I40E_SUCCESS (i40e_lan_hmc.c:299-303). The old claim 'SD table and hardware unchanged on prep failure' was wrong because i40e_prep_remove_sd_bp decrements the backing-page refcount before testing it (i40e_hmc.c:287-291). Function at 293-303. Read in full with the prep function; i40e_remove_sd_bp_new not read.

name: jedec_dimm_attach
prose: Precondition: dev is a jedec_dimm device whose parent is an smbus device; the softc is zeroed by this function. It zeroes the softc and stores dev, smbus, spd_addr and tsod_addr, then reads the SPD DRAM-type byte; on a read error it prints a message and returns that error. DDR3 and DDR4 set type_str and the per-type offsets; any other type prints a message and returns EINVAL. It then fills capacity_mb, the manufacturing year and week, the part number and the serial number, returning the error of the first of jedec_dimm_capacity, jedec_dimm_mfg_date or jedec_dimm_field_to_str that fails, and reads the TSOD-present byte, returning its error if the read fails. On all of these error returns no sysctl has been added and the device description is unchanged, but the softc already holds the fields set so far. If the TSOD-present byte has bit 0x80 set it reads the TSOD manufacturer and device ID words; a failure of either read prints a message and is treated as TSOD absent with rc 0 (not an error); otherwise it looks up a known TSOD name. It then adds the type, capacity, part, serial, mfg_year and mfg_week sysctls; adds the temp sysctl only if a TSOD is present and its IDs matched a known device; if a slotid hint exists it stores a strdup(M_DEVBUF) copy in sc->slotid_str and adds a slotid sysctl; and if a TSOD name or slotid exists it extends the device description with them. It returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the 'SPD/TSOD readable' precondition contradicts the documented smbus error returns and non-fatal TSOD failure paths, so it is removed. Real function at 255-459 (slice 276-526 cut the head). Read in full; callee functions not read. The strdup'd slotid string is not freed in this function (freeing in detach was not checked).

name: kbd_realloc_array
prose: Precondition: Giant is held (GIANT_REQUIRED) and the global keyboard array and its size keyboards are consistent. It computes newsize = rounddown(keyboards + ARRAY_DELTA, ARRAY_DELTA) and allocates a zeroed array of that many keyboard_t pointers with M_NOWAIT; if the allocation fails it returns ENOMEM and leaves the old array and keyboards unchanged. Otherwise it copies the old keyboards entries into the new array, frees the old array only if keyboards > 1 (so that the initial static array is not freed), stores the new array in the global keyboard, sets keyboards to newsize, prints the new size when bootverbose is set and returns 0.
note: Read in full at kbd.c:102-124. The old prose gave ENOMEM as 35; the numeric value is not stated in the code and is removed. ARRAY_DELTA's value was not read. Reviewer reasons were only mechanical.

name: lio_get_set_intr_coalesce
prose: Precondition: arg1 is the struct lio, arg2 selects the coalescing parameter (LIO_USE_ADAPTIVE_RX/TX_COALESCE, LIO_RX_COALESCE_USECS, LIO_RX/TX_MAX_COALESCED_FRAMES, the packet-rate, low/high trigger and sample-interval parameters), req is a sysctl request. For an unrecognised arg2 it returns EINVAL. For each parameter it first loads the current value into both new_val and old_val only under a condition that depends on the parameter: the adaptive-enable flags and the low/high/rate/interval parameters are loaded only when adaptive rx (or tx for the TX ones) is enabled, and the plain RX_COALESCE_USECS and the two MAX_COALESCED_FRAMES parameters only when the corresponding adaptive mode is disabled; otherwise old_val and the value shown remain 0. It calls sysctl_handle_64; if that returns an error or req->newptr is NULL it returns that error (or 0). It returns 0 without changes when the new value equals old_val (so with old_val still 0 a written value of 0 is also treated as no change). Otherwise it applies the value: the adaptive flags are set to 1 or 0; the plain usecs/frames values are held for the hardware step below; the rate, trigger and interval fields are stored in intrmod_cfg only if adaptive rx (or tx, or either for the two rate parameters and the interval) is enabled. It then refreshes rx_usecs, rx_frames and tx_frames in intrmod_cfg from the device configuration and calls lio_set_intrmod_cfg (a failure only logs a message). If adaptive rx is disabled it programs the hardware with lio_intrmod_cfg_rx_intrtime and lio_intrmod_cfg_rx_intrcnt (using the saved values from oct when no new one was given) and returns the first nonzero return value; if adaptive rx is enabled it copies the configured rx values into oct. Likewise if adaptive tx is disabled it calls lio_intrmod_cfg_tx_intrcnt and returns its nonzero result, else copies the configured tx value into oct. It returns 0 if nothing failed.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the no-op test compares against old_val, which is 0 when the load condition is false (lio_sysctl.c:1717-1727, 1746-1755, 1788-1797), so it is not a comparison with the true current value. Round 2 reviewer is right that the tx helper can return a negative errno (stated generally as 'the helper's nonzero return value' because the helper was not read). Original reviewer right that positive and negative values can both be returned. Real function at 1706-1972 (slice 1590-1840 cut the head). Read in full; helpers not read.

name: mana_poll
prose: Precondition: arg is a valid struct mana_cq with a valid gdma_cq (pending is unused). It sets cq->work_done to 0 and cq->budget to MANA_RX_BUDGET for a receive queue (MANA_CQ_TYPE_RX) or MANA_TX_BUDGET otherwise. It then loops at most MANA_POLL_BUDGET times; on the last allowed iteration it first sets cq->budget to CQE_POLLING_BUFFER + 1; each iteration calls mana_cq_handler(cq, cq->gdma_cq) and leaves the loop if cq->work_done < cq->budget, otherwise it resets cq->work_done to 0 and continues. mana_cq_handler polls the RX or TX completions and then always calls mana_gd_ring_cq on the queue, with the arm bit set only when work_done < budget and cq->do_not_ring_db is false (otherwise it rings with arm bit 0). The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: mana_cq_handler rings the doorbell on every call and only the arm bit depends on the condition (mana_en.c:1915-1920), so the old statement that the doorbell may be rung only when the condition holds was wrong. Original reviewer right that arming is not guaranteed when do_not_ring_db is true. Real function at 1927-1955 (slice 1784-2038 cut the head). Read in full with mana_cq_handler (1900-1921); the rx/tx poll routines not read.

name: mfi_dump_blocks
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid softc, len is nonnegative, and virt points to len readable bytes (the data is sent to the device, flags MFI_CMD_DATAOUT). It returns EBUSY if mfi_dequeue_free returns no command, without touching anything else. Otherwise it zeroes the command frame (keeping its context), fills an MFI_CMD_LD_WRITE I/O frame for target id with lba, header data_len = howmany(len, MFI_SECTOR_LEN) (a sector count) and sets cm_data = virt, cm_len = len, and flags MFI_CMD_POLLED | MFI_CMD_DATAOUT. It calls mfi_mapcmd; if that returns nonzero it prints a message. Then in all cases it syncs cm_dmamap with BUS_DMASYNC_POSTWRITE, unloads the DMA map, releases the command and returns the result of mfi_mapcmd (0, or the nonzero error, in which case the write may not have been performed).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the buffer is read (DATAOUT), not written, by the command (mfi.c:2635). Round 2 reviewer's point about rounding the buffer to whole sectors is not supported by the code: cm_len is set to len, only the header data_len is a sector count (2626, 2632); whether the hardware reads beyond len was not determined. Round 1 reviewer right that an mfi_mapcmd error means no completed write. Real function at 2602-2645 (slice 2417-2680). Read in full; mfi_mapcmd not read.

name: mfi_linux_ioctl_int
prose: Precondition: dev->si_drv1 is an initialised mfi softc and arg is a user pointer to a packet whose type depends on cmd. For MFI_LINUX_CMD_2: it copies in a mfi_linux_ioc_packet (returning the copyin error), returns EINVAL if lioc_sge_count > MAX_LINUX_IOCTL_SGE, and returns EBUSY if no free command can be dequeued (these three returns happen before any command, buffer or lock is held). It copies the frame into the command, allocates a zeroed kernel data buffer of the header data_len when a data direction flag is set, and for data-out commands copies each scatter-gather segment from the user iov_base addresses into it (a copyin failure goes to the exit). It takes the config lock for DCMD commands, then under mfi_io_lock calls mfi_check_command_pre and mfi_wait_command (an error from either goes to the exit). For data-in commands it copies the data back out to each segment's user iov_base; if lioc_sense_len is nonzero it copies the command's sense data to the user address taken from the sense offset in the user packet; then it copies the one-byte command status into the user packet's frame header. Any copyout failure goes to the exit. At the exit it unlocks the config lock, frees the data buffer if any, releases the command under mfi_io_lock and returns the error (0 on success). For MFI_LINUX_SET_AEN_2: it copies in the mfi_linux_ioc_aen (returning the copyin error without allocating anything), prints a message, allocates an AEN entry, and under mfi_io_lock inserts it into sc->mfi_aen_pids and calls mfi_aen_register; if that fails the entry is removed and freed; it returns mfi_aen_register's result. For any other cmd it prints a message and returns ENOENT without touching arg.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: read data and sense data go to the user addresses given in the scatter-gather list and the sense pointer (mfi.c:3573-3575, 3598-3599), and only the final one-byte status is written into the user packet (3607-3610); the old text said all three went into the packet. Round 2 reviewer right that a copyin error returns before the AEN entry exists (3629-3631). Original reviewer right that the AEN path does not fill user buffers. Real function at 3462-3656 (slice 3459-3719). Read in full; callees not read.

name: atphy_service
prose: Precondition: sc, mii and mii->mii_media.ifm_cur are valid. MII_POLLSTAT does nothing before the common status update. MII_MEDIACHG: for IFM_AUTO or IFM_1000_T it calls atphy_setmedia and then falls to the common status update; for IFM_100_TX or IFM_10_T it programs the ANAR, clears the gigabit control register when the PHY has gigabit extended capabilities, and writes BMCR with the speed, duplex and reset/autoneg/restart bits; for IFM_NONE it writes BMCR with BMCR_ISO set; any other subtype returns EINVAL immediately with no status update. MII_TICK: if the current media subtype is not IFM_AUTO it sets mii_ticks to 0 and continues; for IFM_AUTO it reads BMSR twice and if the link is up it sets mii_ticks to 0 and continues; if the link is down, the first such tick (mii_ticks was 0) continues without further action, later ticks return 0 immediately, skipping the status update, while mii_ticks (after incrementing) is at most mii_anegticks, and once mii_ticks exceeds mii_anegticks it resets mii_ticks to 0, calls atphy_setmedia and continues. Every path that continues, including all MII_MEDIACHG paths except EINVAL, then calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd) and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: on the first link-down tick (mii_ticks++ == 0) the code breaks and does call PHY_STATUS and mii_phy_update (atphy.c:190-191, 201-204); only later ticks with mii_ticks <= mii_anegticks return early at 192-193. Original reviewer right that the EINVAL and MII_TICK early returns skip the status update. Function at 108-206 (slice 1-260). Read in full; the IFM_NONE branch lines 135-142 were comment-only.

name: gentbi_service
prose: Precondition: sc and mii are valid; cmd is the service command. For MII_POLLSTAT nothing is done before the common update. For MII_MEDIACHG it calls mii_phy_setmedia(sc) and then also continues to the common update. For MII_TICK it calls mii_phy_tick(sc) and returns 0 immediately, skipping the status update, if that returns EJUSTRETURN; otherwise it continues. For any other cmd it continues. On every path that continues it calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd), and returns 0. The function returns 0 on all paths.
note: Both reviewers right: MII_TICK with EJUSTRETURN returns before PHY_STATUS (gentbi.c:196-197), and MII_MEDIACHG falls through to PHY_STATUS and mii_phy_update (191-193, 202-205). Function at 183-207 (slice 1-259). Read in full.

name: e1000phy_service
prose: Precondition: sc, mii and mii->mii_media.ifm_cur are valid. MII_POLLSTAT does nothing before the common update. MII_MEDIACHG: for IFM_AUTO it calls e1000phy_mii_phy_auto; otherwise it chooses the speed from the subtype and returns EINVAL for IFM_1000_T when MIIF_HAVE_GTCR is not set, for IFM_1000_SX when the PHY has neither 1000BASE-X full nor half duplex extended capability, and for any unlisted subtype; IFM_NONE writes E1000_CR with the isolate and power-down bits set and skips the rest; the other speeds write the gigabit control, advertisement and control registers with a reset. MII_TICK: for a non-IFM_AUTO media it sets mii_ticks to 0; for IFM_AUTO it reads BMSR twice, sets mii_ticks to 0 if link is up, and if link is down it increments mii_ticks and acts only once mii_ticks exceeds mii_anegticks, in which case it sets mii_ticks to 0, calls PHY_RESET and e1000phy_mii_phy_auto. Every path that does not return EINVAL then calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd) and returns 0. mii_ticks is modified only on the MII_TICK path.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: only the MII_TICK path changes mii_ticks (e1000phy.c:380-401). Original reviewer right that EINVAL covers any unsupported subtype (349-350), not only the gigabit cases. Real function at 308-413 (slice 255-506 cut the head). Read in full.

name: mlx4_master_do_cmd
prose: Precondition: dev is a master device with priv->mfunc.master.slave_state allocated and slave is a valid index; the caller holds neither slave_state_lock nor cmd.slave_cmd_mutex. It first flips slave_state[slave].comm_toggle and builds reply with the new toggle in bit 31. If the toggle argument differs from the new comm_toggle it goes to the reset_slave path. If cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET it clears active, old_vlan_api and vst_qinq_supported, deactivates the slave admin state and resets each event_eq entry (eqn -1, token 0); if the slave last_cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_FLR it then jumps straight to inform_slave_state, skipping the resource deletion, the shutdown event and the last_cmd update; otherwise it dispatches MLX4_DEV_EVENT_SLAVE_SHUTDOWN, adds the comm version to reply and goes to reset_slave. For a non-RESET cmd received while last_cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_FLR it logs a warning and returns without writing a reply. Otherwise it handles the command in sequence: VHCR0 (requires last_cmd RESET) starts vhcr_dma and clears the cookie; VHCR1 and VHCR2 (each requiring the previous command as last_cmd) add the next address parts; VHCR_EN (requires last_cmd VHCR2) completes vhcr_dma, calls mlx4_master_activate_admin_state (failure goes to reset_slave), sets active and dispatches MLX4_DEV_EVENT_SLAVE_INIT; VHCR_POST (requires last_cmd VHCR_EN or VHCR_POST) calls mlx4_master_process_vhcr(dev, slave, NULL) with slave_cmd_mutex held and released again (a nonzero return goes to reset_slave); an out-of-sequence or unknown command goes to reset_slave. After a handled command it takes slave_state_lock (irqsave) and sets last_cmd to cmd unless the slave is going down, in which case it logs and returns without writing a reply; otherwise it writes reply (just the new toggle bit) to priv->mfunc.comm[slave].slave_read followed by mmiowb. At reset_slave it deletes all resources for the slave if the interface state is UP, adds COMM_CHAN_EVENT_INTERNAL_ERR to reply when cmd is not RESET, sets last_cmd to MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET unless the slave is going down, then at inform_slave_state zeroes the first sizeof(struct mlx4_slave_event_eq_info) bytes of event_eq, writes reply to slave_read and issues wmb. The function returns nothing.
note: Same function as record 34: mlx4_master_do_cmd at mlx4_cmd.c:2096-2232 (slice 1874-2127 started inside it). Round 15 reviewer is right: a RESET received during FLR jumps to inform_slave_state at 2125-2126 without dispatching shutdown. Original reviewer right that the comm_toggle is flipped before it is compared (2106-2108), so the old precondition was wrong. The prose is identical to record 34 on purpose. Read in full; callee functions not read.

The function returns nothing.
note: Same function as record 33: mlx4_master_do_cmd at mlx4_cmd.c:2096-2232. Round 15 reviewer is wrong on both points: toggle mismatch does go to the reset path (2108-2112), and a RESET during FLR does skip resource deletion and the last_cmd update by jumping to inform_slave_state (2125-2126). Original reviewer right that the mid-FLR non-RESET command and the going-down case return without writing a reply (2136-2141, 2196-2200). The old statement that RESET and the other failures all delete resources is corrected: the FLR reset case does not. Read in full; callee functions not read.

name: mlx4_master_process_vhcr
prose: Precondition: dev is a master device, slave a valid slave index, and in_vhcr is either NULL (the vhcr is then read from the slave by DMA with mlx4_ACCESS_MEM and the result is written back to the slave) or a caller-supplied vhcr command buffer. It allocates a software vhcr, returning -ENOMEM if that fails. If in_vhcr is NULL and the DMA read fails it frees the software vhcr and returns that error without writing a status. It decodes the vhcr fields and looks up the command in cmd_info; an unknown opcode sets status CMD_STAT_BAD_PARAM and goes to out_status. For commands with an inbox it allocates a mailbox (failure: CMD_STAT_BAD_SIZE) and reads it from the slave (failure: status CMD_STAT_INTERNAL_ERR, and ret keeps the nonzero DMA error); a failing verify function gives CMD_STAT_BAD_OP; an outbox allocation failure gives CMD_STAT_BAD_SIZE (all of these go to out_status). It then runs the command through its wrapper or, if none, through __mlx4_cmd; an error is converted with mlx4_errno_to_status into vhcr_cmd->status and goes to out_status. On success, if the command has an outbox and status is 0, it DMA-writes the outbox back to the slave; a failure there logs an error and goes to the out label, skipping the vhcr result write-back and returning that error. At out_status, only when in_vhcr is NULL, it DMA-writes the vhcr result back to the slave, overwriting ret with that result (an error is only logged) and generates a command-completion EQE if the e_bit is set and the write-back succeeded. At out it frees the software vhcr, inbox and outbox and returns ret. So command failures are reported through vhcr_cmd->status and the return value is usually 0, but it is nonzero when the initial read, the outbox write-back or the final result write-back fails, and also when an inbox read failure occurred and in_vhcr was non-NULL.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: an inbox read failure sets CMD_STAT_INTERNAL_ERR (mlx4_cmd.c:1752) and ret stays nonzero unless the vhcr result write-back at 1826-1833 overwrites it (it does so only when in_vhcr is NULL). Original reviewer right that the initial read failure returns the transfer error without writing a status (1701-1707). Real function at 1675-1845 (slice 1621-1873). Read in full; the wrappers and __mlx4_cmd not read.

name: mlx4_init_slave
prose: Precondition: dev is a slave function with its comm channel mapped; the caller does not hold priv->cmd.slave_cmd_mutex. It returns -EAGAIN without taking the mutex if the global pf_loading is nonzero. Otherwise it takes slave_cmd_mutex, sets max_cmds to 1 and checks mlx4_comm_check_offline; if the channel is offline it releases the mutex and returns -EIO without sending any command. It then resets the VF support state and sends MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET with mlx4_comm_cmd: if that returns MLX4_DELAY_RESET_SLAVE (the slave is in FLR) it releases the mutex and returns -EAGAIN without sending a further command; any other nonzero result goes to the error exit. It then compares the interface revision from the comm channel with its own and goes to the error exit on a mismatch, and sends VHCR0, VHCR1, VHCR2 and VHCR_EN carrying the 64-bit VHCR DMA address in four parts, going to the error exit if any fails. On success it releases the mutex and returns 0. The error exit sends another MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET (timeout 0, result ignored), releases the mutex and returns -EIO. So -EIO is returned when the channel is offline (no RESET sent), when the first RESET fails for a reason other than FLR delay, on revision mismatch, or when any VHCR command fails (the last three after a second RESET).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the initial RESET failure (non-delay) goes to err and returns -EIO (mlx4_main.c:1991-1997). Original reviewer right that the offline and DELAY_RESET paths return without sending a RESET (1980-1982, 1992-1995). Real function at 1965-2033 (slice 1786-2038). Read in full; mlx4_comm_cmd not read.

name: __mlx4_qp_modify
prose: Precondition: dev, qp and context are valid; mtt must be valid for the RST-to-INIT transition (it is not used otherwise). It returns -EINVAL, issuing nothing, if cur_state or new_state is MLX4_QP_NUM_STATE or more, or if the static op table has no command for that pair. If the command is MLX4_CMD_2RST_QP it issues it directly with mlx4_cmd (no mailbox is allocated on this path) and then, if the device is a master, cur_state is neither MLX4_QP_STATE_ERR nor MLX4_QP_STATE_RST and the QP is the master or proxy QP0 (is_master_qp0), it clears the matching proxy_qp0_active or qp0_active flag of port (qpn & 1) + 1; it then returns the mlx4_cmd result, whether or not the command succeeded. For other commands it allocates a command mailbox and returns PTR_ERR of it on failure. For RST to INIT it fills the MTT base address and log page size in the context; for RTR to RTS it sets roce_entropy when MLX4_DEV_CAP_FLAG2_ROCE_V1_V2 is set. It writes optpar and a copy of the context with local_qpn = qp->qpn into the mailbox and issues the command (op[cur_state][new_state]) with mlx4_cmd. Afterwards, if the device is a master and the QP is a master or proxy QP0, it clears the qp0/proxy_qp0 active flag when the new state is ERR from a state other than ERR or RST, or sets it when the new state is RTR; these updates are made regardless of whether the command succeeded. It frees the mailbox and returns the mlx4_cmd result.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the 2RST_QP command is handled before any mailbox allocation (mlx4_qp.c:145-158). Round 2 reviewer right that the qp0 flags are cleared only when cur_state is neither ERR nor RST on that path (148-150). Original reviewer right about the -EINVAL for undefined transitions (141-143). The flag updates not depending on command success is stated from lines 183-203. Read in full at 88-207.

name: mlx4_QP_FLOW_STEERING_ATTACH_wrapper
prose: Precondition: dev, slave, vhcr, inbox, outbox and cmd describe a flow-steering attach command from the slave; inbox->buf holds a mlx4_net_trans_rule_hw_ctrl followed by the rule header. It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if dev->caps.steering_mode is not MLX4_STEERING_MODE_DEVICE_MANAGED, and -EINVAL if mlx4_slave_convert_port returns a value <= 0 for the control port (otherwise it stores the converted port in the control block). It reads the QP number, takes a reference on the QP resource with get_res and returns its error if that fails (nothing to release yet). It maps the rule header id. If the slave is the device's own function (slave == dev->caps.function) it skips all header checks and goes straight to executing the command. Otherwise by header id: for Ethernet it returns -EINVAL (after releasing the QP) when validate_eth_header_mac fails; IB is accepted; IPv4, TCP and UDP rules get an Ethernet header added with add_eth_header (failure is -EINVAL) and vhcr->in_modifier is increased by the Ethernet header size in 4-byte units; any other id returns -EINVAL. It then issues MLX4_QP_FLOW_STEERING_ATTACH with mlx4_cmd_imm, placing the rule id in vhcr->out_param (a failure returns that error after releasing the QP reference, with no detach). On success it registers the rule as a RES_FS_RULE owned by the slave and bound to qpn with add_res_range, looks it up with get_res, allocates a mirror copy of the inbox in that resource (-ENOMEM on failure), swaps the mirror's port (1 becomes 2, anything else becomes 1), calls mlx4_do_mirror_rule when the device is bonded and increments the QP ref_count. A failure of add_res_range, of the second get_res, or of the allocation, after the attach command succeeded, sends MLX4_QP_FLOW_STEERING_DETACH for the new rule id; this function does not call rem_res_range for a RES_FS_RULE that was already registered. The RES_FS_RULE reference is released with put_res when it was taken, and the QP reference taken by get_res is released with put_res on every path after the QP lookup succeeded. It returns 0 on success or the error described.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: when slave == dev->caps.function the code goes to execute at mlx4_resource_tracker.c:4366-4367 and does not run the header switch, so an unknown header id is not rejected for the function's own slave. Real function at 4326-4447 (slice 4333-4600 cut the head). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: mlx4_ib_mcg_work_handler
prose: Precondition: work is the work member of a valid mcast_group on which a reference is held for this scheduled work; the caller does not hold group->lock. It takes group->lock and starts with a release count rc = 1 (for the scheduled work). If group->state is MCAST_RESP_READY it cancels the timeout work; if the response TID differs from last_req_tid it logs, restores state to prev_state and skips to request processing; otherwise: for a nonzero response status, if the method is GET_RESP and a pending request exists it replies to the slave with that status, removes and frees the first pending request and increments rc (if none exists it only logs), while a DELETE_RESP during demux flushing increments rc; for a zero status it computes the response and current join states, decrements rc for a GET_RESP that moves the group from no joined state to a joined one, increments rc for a non-GET_RESP whose response join state is 0, and in both cases copies the response record into group->rec. After a matching response it sets state to MCAST_IDLE. Then, while the pending list is non-empty and the state is MCAST_IDLE, it takes the first request and adds to rc the return value of handle_leave_req (for a DELETE request) or handle_join_req (otherwise); those values depend on the request and may be 0 or more than 1. If the state is still MCAST_IDLE it computes the join state to leave with get_leave_state; if nonzero it clears those bits in group->rec and sends a leave to the wire: on a send failure it restores the state and increments rc, else the state becomes MCAST_LEAVE_SENT. If requests are still pending and the state is MCAST_IDLE it repeats the request processing. It then releases group->lock and calls release_group(group, 0) rc times (rc can be below 1 after the decrement above, in which case fewer releases are made). The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: join requests need not add 1 to rc since handle_join_req's return value is added (mlx4_ib_mcg.c:719-722). Original reviewer right that group->rec is updated only on a zero-status response (689-704), not on error status. Real function at 642-745 (slice 511-778 cut the head). Read in full; handle_join_req, handle_leave_req, send_leave_to_wire and get_leave_state not read.
